paragraph: In September 2026 Angola's National Director of Registries and Notary Services, Aristides Marques, [said 17,166,000 national identity cards had been issued](<https://angolanewswire.com/angolan-government-issues-more-than-17-million-citizens-identity-cards/>). [Angop reports Cabinda province now issues more than 200 cards a day](<https://angop.ao/en/noticias/sociedade/municipes-destacam-impacto-do-servico-desconcentrado-do-bi-em-cabinda/>). They are delivered in under 24 hours since printing was decentralised in June 2026. In the last twelve months, [a presidential order of August 2026 authorised US$28 million for a digital identity platform](<https://valoreconomico.co.ao/artigo/pr-autoriza-mais-70-milhoes-de-dolares-para-a-transformacao-digital-do-pais>), with capacity for up to 30 million digital identities. No source found since October 2023 says the system checks people by biometrics. Operating would need the system to check fingerprints, face or iris to stop one person enrolling twice.

In August 2026 Burundi's finance ministry [planned to recruit a contractor to set up a national digital identity system](<https://armp.gov.bi/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/PPM-finances-budgetaire-2026-2027-final.docx-Revise1.pdf>). The plan carries BIF 8,902,999,980 on the state budget. [On 6 May 2026 the interior ministry presented the card and its unique number as a project not yet issued](<https://www.sosmediasburundi.org/2026/05/11/burundi-la-carte-didentite-biometrique-encore-loin-detre-une-realite/>), SOS Médias Burundi reports. In the last twelve months, [the President said in December 2025 that the system was being tested in Zone Matara, Gitega province](<https://communityvoice.bi/the-lack-of-digital-id-systems-threatens-the-digital-economy-of-burundi/>). In May 2026 an official said [Burundi was technically ready to produce the cards, with issuance waiting on a law](<https://lionweek.com/burundi-seeks-saudi-support-for-digital-id-and-data-centre-at-doha-telecoms-summit/>). No source found since October 2023 says the system is in service. Establishing would need the national ID system in service, issuing each person a unique number or credential.

In September 2026 the national agency ANIP [said the biometric national identity card (CNIB) is issued, certifying identity from the holder's personal identification number](<https://beninwebtv.com/benin-la-carte-didentite-biometrique-peut-desormais-etre-renouvelee-en-ligne/>). [ANIP director Aristide Adjinacou refers to the Registre national des personnes physiques and the personal identification number (NPI)](<https://www.lanation.bj/actualites/aristide-adjinacou-directeur-general-de-lanip-nous-voulons-faire-de-chaque-maternite-une-veritable-porte-dentree-vers-lidentite-legale>). In the last twelve months, ANIP let holders start renewing the card online, in September 2026. [In October 2026 pensioners proved they were alive at biometric kiosks and in an app, using their biometric identity card and NPI](<https://lanouvelletribune.info/2026/10/benin-15-189-retraites-ont-deja-effectue-leur-preuve-de-vie-la-campagne-se-poursuit/>). No source found since October 2023 says the system checks people by biometrics. Operating would need the system to check fingerprints, face or iris to stop one person enrolling twice.

The national police's 2026 CNIB page says the Office national d'identification (ONI) [checks for duplicate identities by matching fingerprints](<https://www.police.gov.bf/index.php/infos-utiles/cnib>), and [has matched faces too since 2009](<https://www.police.gov.bf/index.php/infos-utiles/cnib>). In the last twelve months, [on 11 November 2026 President Traoré launched mass enrolment for a unique identifier](<https://www.sidwaya.info/2026/11/11/operation-denregistrement-de-masse-de-lidentifiant-unique-le-capitaine-ibrahim-traore-lance-loperation-denrolement/>). The number is free, random and 12 digits long. Enrolment for it takes a photograph, fingerprints and iris to eliminate multiple records, the Presidency says. [From 16 October 2026 the Gendarmerie's brigades also produce the card](<https://aconews.net/burkina-faso-desormais-la-gendarmerie-nationale-produit-les-cib-aes-et-legalise-les-documents-administratifs/>). No source found since October 2023 reports a certification, audit or assurance level for the system. Mature would need a security certification, audit or assurance level, and the ID held by all or nearly all the population.

In September 2026 the Bankers' Association of Botswana [launched a national eKYC project letting banks verify customer identities against the national citizen database](<https://www.businesstechafrica.co.za/article/botswana-launches-national-ekyc-project-to-make-bank-verification-easier>). A 2021 system verified identity cards the same way. In the last twelve months, [in October 2026 the minister said nearly half of the 45,000 Omang cards needed to clear a production backlog had been made](<https://dailynews.gov.bw/news-detail/93807>). [The minister's electoral reform package proposes maintaining the Omang as the primary form of ID](<https://allafrica.com/stories/202608190305.html>). No source found since October 2023 says the system checks people by biometrics. Operating would need the system to check fingerprints, face or iris to stop one person enrolling twice.

In June 2026 [Corbeau News Centrafrique reported that national identity cards are being issued through police and registry offices in Ndele and other towns, including Bangui](<https://corbeaunews-centrafrique.org/centrafrique-le-business-de-la-carte-nationale-didentite-reprend-de-plus-belle-a-ndele/>). [Journal de Bangui reports that Al-Madina's team is enrolling applicants for the secure national identity card in Birao](<https://www.journaldebangui.com/rca-carte-nationale-didentite-la-societe-al-madina-deploie-sa-mission-a-birao>), after Bouar and Berberati. It captures biometric data. [The $13m SNID, built around a unique identification number, has had feasibility studies done](<https://ambition-journal.org/fr/economie/systeme-national-d-identite-numerique-moderniser-l-administration>). Implementation is planned for 2027-2032. In the last twelve months, applicants told that June 2026 report they were asked to pay 100,000 to 200,000 CFA francs for a card. No source found since October 2023 says the system checks people by biometrics. Operating would need the system to check fingerprints, face or iris to stop one person enrolling twice.

[ONECI attributed 9,323,415 national identification numbers in 2025](<https://www.koaci.com/article/2026/02/10/cote-divoire/societe/cote-divoire-le-delai-de-delivrance-de-la-carte-nationale-didentite-ramene-a-moins-de-deux-semaines-perspectives-de-la-structure-pour-2026_194217.html>). [ONECI manages the RNPP and assigns the national identification number, the PARAE coordinator says](<https://www.aip.ci/cote-divoire-aip-le-gouvernement-mise-sur-le-parae-pour-renforcer-la-confiance-dans-les-services-publics-numeriques/>). [The RNPP holds citizens' biometric and civil data](<https://digitalmag.ci/identite-numerique-la-cote-divoire-pays-connecte-mais-pas-encore-pleinement-identifie/>). In the last twelve months, [in May 2026 ONECI opened an enrolment centre at the embassy in Madrid, its 14th abroad](<https://www.oneci.ci/actualites/1779110716>). In November 2026 ONECI [opened enrolment for the identity card to children from the age of 5](<https://www.linfodrome.com/societe/127887-reforme-de-la-cni-l-oneci-ouvre-ses-acces-aux-enfants-de-5-ans>). No source found since October 2023 says the system checks people by biometrics. Operating would need the system to check fingerprints, face or iris to stop one person enrolling twice.

In February 2025 [Cameroon launched its new biometric national ID card system](<https://www.biometricupdate.com/202508/new-biometric-id-card-center-opens-for-citizens-in-northern-cameroon>), with production centres in Douala and Garoua. [Biometric Update reports the system went live on 17 February 2025 with online pre-enrolment](<https://www.biometricupdate.com/202503/cameroon-opens-new-id-card-production-centre-as-issuance-gains-traction>), and the first cards were given to applicants on 3 March 2025. In the last twelve months, [the Yaounde 5 mayor handed out 4,000 free national identity cards on 27 July 2026](<https://tribunedelinfo.com/de-la-promesse-a-la-cni-en-main-4000-beneficiaires-soulages-a-yaounde-5/>). DGSN police officers had worked on site to clear double-identity cases. No source found since October 2023 says the system checks people by biometrics. Operating would need the system to check fingerprints, face or iris to stop one person enrolling twice.

[ONIP resumed issuing the biometric national ID card in April 2024, in four pilot Kinshasa communes](<https://www.bbc.com/afrique/articles/cy633p6ezq1o>). In the last twelve months, [RDC-PASS, launched in June 2026, entered a first operational phase that September](<https://www.agenceecofin.com/actualites-numerique/3009-142019-rdc-strategies-identite-numerique-et-cybersecurite-au-bilan-d-un-an-de-reformes>). On 11 September 2026 the interior minister [told the Council of Ministers that ONIP's mass identification would launch in mid-December](<https://actualite.cd/2026/09/16/rdc-lidentification-de-masse-de-la-population-annoncee-pour-mi-decembre-2026>). [By September 2026 mass enrolment had not reached provinces such as Tshopo, a civil-society group said](<https://lumiernews.net/carte-didentite-nationale-en-rdc-ou-en-est-le-projet-trois-ans-apres-la-premiere-carte-remise-a-felix-tshisekedi/>). No source found since October 2023 says the card or number is issued beyond pilot communes. Establishing would need the national ID system in service, issuing each person a unique number or credential.

In October 2025 the finance ministry said that enrolment for the NIU [takes iris and fingerprints, in person](<https://www.finances.gouv.cg/en/node/4803>), and that its database held over 600,000 people. The finance minister said the aim is one identity for each taxpayer, to limit duplicates and fraud. [The finance ministry issues the NIU, a unique identification number, to every resident from age 6](<https://www.finances.gouv.cg/fr/articles/relance-des-operations-de-production-de-la-carte-niu>). It is valid for ten years. Card production had restarted in September 2025. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No certification, audit or assurance level for the system has been found since October 2023. Mature would need a security certification, audit or assurance level, and the ID held by all or nearly all the population.

On 31 March 2026 [GenKey took over production of Comorian biometric passports and national identity cards, Al-Watwan reports](<https://alwatwan.net/societe/production-de-documents-biom%C3%A9triques-genkey-succ%C3%A8de-officiellement-%C3%A0-semlex.html>). Semlex had held the concession from 2007, and [issuance was suspended until 26 March 2026 during the change](<https://www.biometricupdate.com/202603/genkey-takes-over-biometric-passport-national-id-card-production-in-comoros>). In the last twelve months, [on 25 March 2026 Comoros authorities validated preparatory studies in Moroni for digitising the civil registry](<https://www.wearetech.africa/en/fils-uk/news/tech/comoros-advances-digital-identity-reform-with-nationwide-registry-overhaul>). The work introduces a unique Personal Identification Number as the cornerstone of citizen identity. No source found since October 2023 says the system checks people by biometrics. Operating would need the system to check fingerprints, face or iris to stop one person enrolling twice.

In May 2026 [Biometric Update reported that Cabo Verde issues a Unique Identification Number to every child born](<https://www.biometricupdate.com/202605/cabo-verdes-crvs-id-reforms-drive-near-universal-birth-registration>). [IMIJ states SNIAC has contributed to issuing about 631,720 national identity cards, 513,862 electronic passports and 14,235 residence permits](<https://imij.gov.cv/noticias/cms-noticia-24>) since its implementation. [The Autentika portal says citizens authenticate to services with the smart-card national identity card and its PIN](<https://portal-autentika.gov.cv/>). The card is activated in person at registry offices, the Casa do Cidadão and consulates. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the system checks people by biometrics. Operating would need the system to check fingerprints, face or iris to stop one person enrolling twice.

In July 2026 the head of the NNI service said that [fingerprints, iris and photograph are captured and automatically compared with the database](<https://www.lanation.dj/carte-nationale-didentite-biometrique-dans-les-coulisses-de-la-nouvelle-identite-nationale/>). The comparison has detected duplicates and people using a dead person's identity. In the last twelve months, [Djibouti's President launched the Mobile ID digital identity platform on 9 February 2026](<https://www.wearetech.africa/en/fils-uk/news/tech/djibouti-officially-launches-mobile-id-digital-identity-platform>), with biometric data held by the Interior Ministry. [The Interior Ministry says it launched Mobile ID on 10 February 2026 as the national secure digital identity system](<https://interieur.gouv.dj/forum-sur-lidentite-numerique-et-lancement-du-projet-mobile-id/>). No source found since October 2023 reports a certification, audit or assurance level for the system. Mature would need a security certification, audit or assurance level, and the ID held by all or nearly all the population.

In May 2026 the Ministry of the Interior said [identity and travel documents are issued only after fingerprint matching](<https://id4africa.com/2026/files/T2-3-S3-4-Algeria-FINAL.pdf>), and that its issuance system is connected to AFIS. The ministry says the biometric electronic national ID card (CNIBE) has been issued since January 2016. More than 40 million cards are in circulation. In the last twelve months, [citizens holding the national digital identity issued by the Haut Commissariat a la Numerisation can access the WADHIFATI platform without a separate account](<https://www.horizons.dz/2026/08/les-plateformes-du-ministere-des-sports-integrees-dans-lecosysteme-national-des-services-numeriques/>). No source found since October 2023 reports a certification, audit or assurance level for the system. Mature would need a security certification, audit or assurance level, and the ID held by all or nearly all the population.

In July 2026 [the Public Prosecution's online service verified enquirers through the digital identity system](<https://gate.ahram.org.eg/News/5838334.aspx>), with its records keyed to the national number. [The National ID System runs a card production centre and issuing centres](<https://www.citc.com.eg/National%20ID%20SYSTEM.html>), and its databases hold citizens' images and fingerprints. In the last twelve months, [the communications ministry has been building a unified national 'digital identity' for the whole state, says the NTRA's chief](<https://gate.ahram.org.eg/News/5887018.aspx>). Full operation of that national digital identity is still to come. No source found since October 2023 says the system checks people by biometrics. Operating would need the system to check fingerprints, face or iris to stop one person enrolling twice.

In March 2026 [the UK Home Office guidance said Eritrea issues national ID cards, which are required for an Eritrean passport](<https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/eritrea-knowledge-base-profile/eritrea-knowledge-base-profile>). [The Eritrean embassy in Washington says Eritreans aged 18 or above must obtain a national ID](<https://us.embassyeritrea.org/national-id/>). [In late 2015 Eritrea began issuing plastic national identity cards carrying the holder's fingerprint, the US State Department says](<https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/us-visas/Visa-Reciprocity-and-Civil-Documents-by-Country/Eritrea.html>). It said very few were in circulation. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the system checks people by biometrics. Operating would need the system to check fingerprints, face or iris to stop one person enrolling twice.

In March 2025 the national ID programme said Fayda [takes iris, ten fingerprints and a face image to identify each person uniquely](<https://www.bbc.com/amharic/articles/c204dl15p96o>). It works on a principle of one person, one ID. In the last twelve months, [Fayda recorded more than 52 million registrations and over 208 million eKYC verifications as of 9 October 2026](<https://www.biometricupdate.com/202610/ethiopia-launches-developer-sandbox-to-support-fayda-digital-id-innovation-integration>). It was launched at scale in 2023. [By mid-November 2026 more than 53 million Ethiopians held a Fayda ID, Fana reports](<https://www.fanamc.com/archives/326470>). No source found since October 2023 reports a certification, audit or assurance level for the system. Mature would need a security certification, audit or assurance level, and the ID held by all or nearly all the population.

In June 2026 [the Interior Minister told the National Assembly that 164,944 CNIE cards have been produced and 147,224 collected by holders](<https://africacoeurnews.com/2026/06/03/gabon-17720-cartes-didentite-electroniques-toujours-non-retirees/>). They come from the enrolment campaign begun in 2024. [Gabon launched a new generation national digital ID system in July 2024](<https://www.biometricupdate.com/202609/gabon-ramping-up-digital-id-interoperability-infrastructure-implementation>), which the government says it is now moving to operationalise. In the last twelve months, [the sixth e-Gabon-SIS steering committee on 8 September 2026 reviewed the deployment of a National Digital Identity System](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/09/09/gabon-four-digital-projects-modernise-public-services/>), per ANINF. No source found since October 2023 says the system checks people by biometrics. Operating would need the system to check fingerprints, face or iris to stop one person enrolling twice.

By 30 October 2026 the National Identification Authority had [enrolled 20,610,948 people and issued 19,575,078 cards](<https://ghana.dubawa.org/false-91-of-ghanaians-have-not-received-their-ghana-cards/>). In the last twelve months its count rose from [18,955,360 people registered and 17,855,708 cards issued by September 2025](<https://kessbenonline.com/2025/09/16/nia-to-mandate-biometric-verification-for-public-services/>). In September 2026 it [began registering children aged six to 14](<https://www.modernghana.com/news/1528541/ghana-card-to-become-e-wallet-for-electronic-trans.html>). In August 2026 [its Labone centre registered around the clock in three shifts](<https://thehighstreetjournal.com/nia-adopts-three-shift-system-for-24-hour-ghana-card-registration/>). No source found since October 2023 says the system checks people by biometrics. Operating would need the system to check fingerprints, face or iris to stop one person enrolling twice.

In April 2025 the government [received 3,000 biometric enrolment kits](<https://gouvernement.gov.gn/le-premier-ministre-receptionne-les-kits-denrolement-biometrique/>) and said the kits, with fingerprint sensors and iris recognition, guarantee that each citizen is unique. Enrolment of people aged 10 and over [was launched on 15 April 2025](<https://mediaguinee.com/2025/04/en-avant-pour-le-recensement-biometrique-par-sayon-mara/>). In the last twelve months, ID Tech Wire reported in March 2026 that [enrolment for the biometric national ID card had begun](<https://idtechwire.com/guinea-launches-biometric-birth-certificates-in-sanoyah-in-civil-registry-modernization-push>) in Sanoyah commune. In September 2026 the territorial administration minister [opened work on extending the register](<https://www.guinee114.com/2026/09/18/matd-dge-djenabou-toure-lance-latelier-sur-lextension-du-registre-national-des-personnes-physiques/>). No source found since October 2023 says the system checks fingerprints, face or iris to stop one person enrolling twice. Operating would need the system to check fingerprints, face or iris to stop one person enrolling twice.

[Public registration for the new biometric national ID card opened on 4 August 2026 in Greater Banjul](<https://foroyaa.net/gambians-welcome-biometric-id-rollout/>). It runs under the National Identity Management System launched 30 June 2026. The government says the system combines a national identity register with biometric technology to reduce duplicate identities and fraud. In the last twelve months, [the Ministry of Interior launched nationwide issuance of a new 10-year biometric National Identity Card on 4 August 2026](<https://www.voicegambia.com/gambia-rolls-out-new-10-year-national-identity-cards/>). No source found since October 2023 reports a certification, audit or assurance level for the system. Mature would need a security certification, audit or assurance level, and the ID held by all or nearly all the population.

In July 2024 Semlex, which runs enrolment, said that [the card system rests on biometric enrolment and a deduplication system](<https://www.semlex.com/en/2024/07/01/nouveau-centre-denrolement-a-bissau/>). That system assigns each citizen a unique identity number. In the last twelve months, [Semlex says its subsidiary opened a third biometric ID enrolment centre in Cacheu region (Sao Domingos) on 26 February 2026](<https://www.semlex.com/2026/03/09/inauguration-du-centre-denrolement-de-sao-domingos/>). [Semlex says Guinea-Bissau has 18 production centres for biometric national ID cards](<https://www.semlex.com/en/2026/02/11/semlex-guinee-bissau-renforce-lacces-a-lidentification-biometrique>). The newest, at Safim, opened on 30 January 2026. No source found since October 2023 reports a certification, audit or assurance level for the system. Mature would need a security certification, audit or assurance level, and the ID held by all or nearly all the population.

In 2024 [CNEDOGE issued national identity documents (DIP) with a biometric security system](<https://www.hayderechoenguinea.com/noticias/sociedad/sobre-el-funcionamiento-del-centro-nacional-de-emision-de-documentos-oficia>), each taking about 30 working days by an unwritten norm. In the last twelve months, [on 15 October 2026 the Vice-President ordered its technology, mostly installed in 2017 and 2018, assessed for modernisation](<https://www.guineaecuatorialpress.com/noticias/el_vicepresidente_de_la_republica_impulsa_la_modernizacion_del_sistema_informatico_de_cnedoge>). The government's press office says the equipment shows wear and limited capacity. CETIS, its supplier, is to say what can be kept and what replaced. No source found since October 2023 says the system checks people by biometrics. Operating would need the system to check fingerprints, face or iris to stop one person enrolling twice.

In May 2026 The Elephant reported that [AFIS checks fingerprints and flags duplicate or fraudulent registrations](<https://www.theelephant.info/investigations/2026/05/28/project-profile-the-in-between-lives-of-the-double-registered/>) as ID applications are processed. The government's deck for ID4Africa 2026 lists [AFIS deduplication in the identity lifecycle](<https://id4africa.com/2026/files/T1-1-3-Kenya-FINAL.pdf>). In the last twelve months, [on 5 November 2026 the immigration department told parliament that at least 557,000 printed cards were uncollected](<https://nation.africa/kenya/news/state-turns-to-chiefs-e-citizen-to-trace-owners-of-uncollected-ids-5660290>). In August 2026 KBC reported that [the High Court had halted the introduction of the Maisha Card](<https://swahili.kbc.co.ke/mahakama-kuu-yapiga-breki-matumizi-ya-maisha-card/>). The halt lasts until a petition against it is decided. No source found since October 2023 reports a certification, audit or assurance level for the system. Mature would need a security certification, audit or assurance level, and the ID held by all or nearly all the population.

In September 2026 a presidential proclamation said [about 720,000 people are enrolled in the NBIS](<https://www.africa-newsroom.com/press/liberia-president-boakai-declares-wednesday-september-16-as-national-identification-day?lang=en>), and required every person in Liberia to enrol. [The registry holds about 740,000 records on a system built by Techno Brain](<https://www.newerainquirer.com/article/29a1a5b7-1ba2-4dde-a435-3dae7102b0f6>). In the last twelve months, [a US$54.7 million concession with OeSD International GmbH covering biometric enrolment, deduplication and digital credentials](<https://allafrica.com/stories/202609080549.html>) was signed and awaited ratification, NIR Executive Director Andrew Peters said on 4 September 2026. [The House sent it to a joint committee on 13 October 2026](<https://www.liberianobserver.com/politics/house-begins-review-of-boakai-s-proposed-national-digital-id-overhaul/article_0c964a7e-9e8c-4c1e-9e05-46bfae096890.html>). [On 18 November 2026 the House endorsed the committees' report recommending its rejection](<https://frontpageafricaonline.com/liberia-house-committee-seeks-rejection-of-oesd-id-concession-over-40-identified-legal-and-financial-defects/>). No source found since October 2023 says the system checks people by biometrics. Operating would need the system to check fingerprints, face or iris to stop one person enrolling twice.

[The Civil Status Authority has issued national numbers through a unified electronic system since 2011](<https://alwasat.ly/news/479468>), each meant as a unique reference for one citizen. In the last twelve months, [in October 2026 the Attorney General's Office found 315,385 National Numbers granted contrary to law](<https://alwasat.ly/news/481677>). [It suspended 8,662 of them](<https://libyaobserver.ly/news/libyas-attorney-general-reveals-315000-unlawfully-issued-national-id-numbers-citizenship-data>). [In April 2026 the Digital Identity Management System for Citizens, whose Level 3 identity is based on biometric data, was in technical trials with the Central Bank of Libya and several banks](<https://www.gia.gov.ly/en/2026/04/19/general-information-authority-central-bank-of-libya-national-authority-for-combating-money-laundering-with-the-relevant-authorities/>). No source found since October 2023 says the national numbers are checked for duplicates by biometrics. Operating would need the system to check fingerprints, face or iris to stop one person enrolling twice.

[The director of the National Identity and Civil Registry says an integrated system launched in 2013 gives each person in the register a unique number](<https://www.uneca.org/eca-events/stories/linking-civil-registration-vital-statistics-and-legal-identity-system-essential-inclusive>). In August 2025 [Lesotho migrants in South Africa used their national digital IDs for formal remittances](<https://www.codevelop.fund/insights-1/strategic-collaboration-establishes-africas-first-cross-border-digital-identity-framework-enabling-financial-inclusion-for-millions>), in a pilot. In the last twelve months, [a 2026 work plan with MICSTI and UNICEF supports an Integrated National Digital Identity Ecosystem for 2026-2030](<https://www.gov.ls/government/micsti-and-unicef-signed-digital-id-work-plan/>). The plan provides for biometric registration and continued MOSIP-based deployment. No source found since October 2023 says the system checks people by biometrics. Operating would need the system to check fingerprints, face or iris to stop one person enrolling twice.

No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the system checks people by biometrics. Operating would need the system to check fingerprints, face or iris to stop one person enrolling twice.
